title: Add a source-bound baseline for the selected productive-helper schema
body:
The selected #4359 certificate uses productive-helper budget stages. The documented historical baseline authenticates its sources, then crashes on `KeyError: 'bit_lower'`. This adds an explicit successor command that reads that schema and reports its compiler, ordinary/admitted BIT and nine-row outer budgets separately.

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_selected_baseline.py
```

The new command authenticates the entire selected closure with the existing checker before printing success. It reports the exact outer minimum **115098849/50000000000**, binding row **main_transform**, and strict slack **98849/50000000000** over selected **23/10000**. It retains symbolic template ranks and does not infer the old balanced-transfer cap.

Only three files are added: the command, 13 focused tests and [usage/scope documentation](https://github.com/mihir-s-05/integer-mult-bounds/blob/108509ac7a441617e3783fbd991bdf249fd23e64/docs/research/selected-baseline.md). All existing files, scientific inputs and selected records remain unchanged. [#3725](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3725) documents why the old helper and its pinned documentation should not be edited casually. [#4436](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4436) already owns the separate current-status/CI navigation repair.

**Validation at 108509ac7a441617e3783fbd991bdf249fd23e64, Windows / CPython 3.12.0:**

- All 13 focused tests pass. They exercise exact stage labels, ties, unsupported schemas, duplicate/missing templates, invalid budgets, omitted outer rows, inconsistent minimum/slack and nonstrict endpoints. Synthetic complete source closures exercise the real checker and CLI in ordinary and optimized Python, including altered sources/proofs and an authenticated but inconsistent certificate.
- The actual selected source checker passes; real-source ordinary and optimized reports are byte-identical. Selected-record SHA256: `5732707cc1e460b090b53f2463162749ad860de878a18f7408938671d295a9d9`.
- Changed-package planning selects **zero** existing packages. Committed-byte comparison for all three added files and `git diff --check` pass.
- The broader Windows/sparse onboarding run is **not green**: 331 tests, 8 failures, 32 errors, 15 skips. Diagnostics include Windows-invalid newline filenames, locale/broken-pipe issues, one Bash timeout, omitted unrelated sparse fixtures and the unchanged status assertions. The four status/navigation failures were separately reproduced on unchanged main before implementation. This PR does not claim a complete onboarding or hosted CI pass.

Focused reproduction:

```sh
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_research_selected_baseline.py -v
```

**Scope and coordination:** `portable-replay`, priority revision 7, explicitly changed from an environment mismatch to the selected certificate-format mismatch in the card's startup command. Canonical main started and refreshed at `2a13eb1827784206202db90e5dc8327cf8a250db`. [Discussion #4458](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4458) is the canonical investigation. Submission overlap coverage: all 5,731 tracked local note paths, 314 open PR bodies, 3,313 Discussion records and 3,787 closed PR bodies, complete pagination at 22:52–22:54 UTC. This is bounded text coverage, not a novelty claim or exhaustive diff search.

**Limitations / next task:** this is source binding and metadata consistency, not native replay, supplier admission or a theorem proof; no new kappa. The pinned catalogue/brief still name the historical command. Their migration needs a source-receipt policy; the new usage note supplies the replacement now. Future certificate schemas need explicit adapters. No selected cold replay was run.

Credit Douglas Colkitt and the retained checker contributors; zxv, Jacob Alan Sussman and the full #4359 contributor map for the scientific data; Mister-Meeseeks and the credited Claude agent in #3725 for the immutable-helper precedent. Prepared by Mihir Srivastava (@mihir-s-05) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents. Apache-2.0.
